proposedTests.name: Create returns 7-char base62 code and copyable short URL
proposedTests.steps: POST /links with a valid absolute https URL; assert 200, JSON body has 'code' matching ^[0-9A-Za-z]{7}$ and 'short_url' non-empty and copyable (path or absolute).
proposedTests.proves: Happy-path create contract and code shape.
proposedTests.determinism: Assert shape only, not specific code value.

proposedTests.name: Same long URL twice yields two distinct codes, both redirect
proposedTests.steps: POST same URL twice; assert two 200s with different codes; GET each code; assert 302 with Location equal to the original URL.
proposedTests.proves: No dedup; both codes resolve to the same target.

proposedTests.name: Missing/empty URL rejected with 400 and no row
proposedTests.steps: POST with no body, empty body, url='' (form and JSON); assert 400 each; assert store.count() unchanged.
proposedTests.proves: Negative boundary for empty input; no side effect.

proposedTests.name: Non-absolute and non-http(s) URLs rejected with 400 and no row
proposedTests.steps: POST values: 'example.com', '/path', 'ftp://x/y', 'javascript:alert(1)', 'http://', 'https://', 'mailto:a@b'; assert 400 each; assert store.count() unchanged.
proposedTests.proves: Scheme and absoluteness boundary; no side effect.

proposedTests.name: Known code returns 302 with exact Location
proposedTests.steps: Create link; GET /{code} with redirects disabled; assert 302 and Location header equals stored long URL exactly.

proposedTests.name: Unknown code returns 404 with no Location
proposedTests.steps: GET /zzzzzzz (7 base62 chars, never created); assert 404 and no Location header.
proposedTests.proves: Negative follow path; no redirect issued.

proposedTests.name: Follow path performs no writes
proposedTests.steps: Create link; snapshot store.count() and DB file mtime/size; GET code N times; assert count unchanged and no new tables/rows; optionally wrap sqlite connection to assert only SELECT executed.
proposedTests.proves: Read-only follow; no click data recorded or exposed.

proposedTests.name: Links do not expire and have no click limit
proposedTests.steps: Create link; follow it 1000 times; assert every response is 302 with same Location; no time-based expiry logic present.

proposedTests.name: Forced collision yields a different code
proposedTests.steps: Inject a generator/store stub where first insert raises CodeCollision; assert generator retries and returns a different code; assert final store row maps new code to the URL.

proposedTests.name: Retry-limit exhaustion returns 500, not infinite loop
proposedTests.steps: Stub store to always raise CodeCollision; assert CodeGenerationError raised within bounded attempts and HTTP layer maps it to 500.

proposedTests.name: Code maps to exactly one long URL
proposedTests.steps: Create link A; attempt direct store.insert(same_code, other_url); assert CodeCollision; GET code; assert Location == A's URL.
proposedTests.proves: UNIQUE constraint is authoritative; no overwrite.

proposedTests.name: Restart persistence
proposedTests.steps: Run 1: start server on temp SQLite file, create link, stop server. Run 2: start server on same file, GET code; assert 302 with original Location.

proposedTests.name: Fresh DB bootstrap is idempotent
proposedTests.steps: Start service against a nonexistent path; assert schema created and create+follow work. Start again on same file; assert no error and prior links still resolve.
proposedTests.proves: Schema creation on first start; idempotent restart.

proposedTests.name: Offline suite passes with no outbound network
proposedTests.steps: Run full suite in a container with outbound network blocked (e.g., no default route or firewall drop); assert all create/follow tests pass; assert no DNS/socket calls to external hosts.

proposedTests.name: Concurrent creates of same URL produce distinct codes and consistent redirects
proposedTests.steps: Fire N parallel POST /links with the same URL; assert N distinct codes; GET each; assert each 302 to the URL; assert store.count() == N.
proposedTests.proves: Threaded server + shared SQLite connection handle concurrency without corruption.

proposedTests.name: Malformed and oversized request bodies
proposedTests.steps: POST with invalid Content-Length, body > MAX_BODY_BYTES, malformed JSON, JSON array, JSON with non-string url; assert 400 each and no row written.
proposedTests.proves: Parser failure handling; no side effects.

proposedTests.name: Path edge cases on follow
proposedTests.steps: GET '/', '/links', '/a/b', '/{code}?x=1', '/{code}#frag'; assert 404 for non-code paths and 302 for code with query/fragment stripped.

observedEvidence.observation: Author reports the full suite was run offline and previously failing HTTP tests now receive a status line and headers instead of RemoteDisconnected.
observedEvidence.status: reported, not independently observed by QA

observedEvidence.observation: protocol_version='HTTP/1.1' with explicit Content-Length added; sqlite3 connection opened with check_same_thread=False.
observedEvidence.status: code inspection only; runtime behavior unverified here

observedEvidence.observation: lookup issues only SELECT; no INSERT/UPDATE on follow path in code.
build_short_url returns path-only '/{code}', which is an allowed form per requirements assumptions.

coverageGaps.gap: No test asserts the exact base62 alphabet used; PT-1 only checks [0-9A-Za-z]{7}. If the implementer's alphabet differs (e.g., includes '-' or '_'), S-1-1 would be violated but PT-1 would pass.
coverageGaps.action: Confirm alphabet with implementer, then tighten PT-1 regex.

coverageGaps.gap: No test verifies that the short URL returned is actually followable end-to-end from the response body alone (PT-1 checks shape, PT-2 uses the code).
coverageGaps.action: Add a test that parses short_url from the create response and GETs it.

coverageGaps.gap: Concurrency test PT-15 is proposed but not observed; the shared sqlite3 connection with check_same_thread=False is not proven safe under parallel writes (SQLite serializes, but WAL + single connection may still raise 'database is locked' under load).
coverageGaps.action: Run PT-15 with N>=20 and assert no 5xx.

coverageGaps.gap: No test covers the 500 path from CodeGenerationError at the HTTP layer (PT-10 covers unit only).
coverageGaps.action: Add integration test with a stub generator that exhausts retries.

coverageGaps.gap: No test asserts that a 400 response body is empty or that no Location header is set on 400/404.
coverageGaps.action: Add header assertions to PT-3, PT-4, PT-6.

coverageGaps.gap: S-2-4 'no click data exposed' is only checked via absence of writes; no test asserts no statistics/listing endpoint exists.
coverageGaps.action: Add a test that GET /stats or similar returns 404.

coverageGaps.gap: Host header spoofing risk noted in design; build_short_url ignores host and returns path, so risk is mitigated, but no test asserts the returned short_url is path-only (or absolute) consistently.
No test verifies behavior when the SQLite file is read-only or corrupt (failure handling).
coverageGaps.action: Add negative test expecting 5xx, not a hang.

failureDetails.risk: ThreadingHTTPServer serves each request on a new thread sharing one sqlite3 connection. Even with check_same_thread=False, concurrent writes can raise sqlite3.OperationalError('database is locked') if WAL busy timeout is not set, producing 500s under load.
failureDetails.expected: All concurrent creates return 200 with distinct codes.

failureDetails.risk: CodeGenerationError is caught in do_POST and mapped to 500, but the retry limit value is an implementer choice; if unbounded, PT-10 will hang.

build_short_url ignores the Host header and returns '/{code}'. If a client expects an absolute URL, S-1-3 'copyable form' may be judged insufficient by a reviewer, though requirements assumptions allow path-only.
failureDetails.expected: Path-only is acceptable per assumptions; flag for reviewer confirmation.

failureDetails.risk: parse_long_url decodes with errors='replace'; a body with invalid UTF-8 may produce a string that passes or fails validation unpredictably.
